$comment: Stripe product/price seed for paid plans + one-time Event Pass. Idempotent source of truth: `npm run stripe:sync` ensures each product + price exists in the Stripe account of STRIPE_SECRET_KEY (matched by price lookup_key), keeps multi-currency price points (currency_options) in sync on every run, and writes the resulting price ids into the `plans` table (stripe_price_id_monthly/annual, stripe_price_id_onetime for passes). Re-run after any DB wipe, and against each environment (test/prod) by pointing STRIPE_SECRET_KEY + DATABASE_URL at it. Non-USD amounts are SET price points (v3/07 §4), never FX conversions. Community is free (no Stripe). Entitlements v18 (2026-09-03): FOUR currencies, not five — AUD was withdrawn outright, plans and registration entry fees alike, and `lib/currency.ts`'s SUPPORTED_CURRENCIES is the list this file must agree with (a `currency_options` key with no entry there, or the reverse, renders one currency's symbol over another currency's number). W3 (2026-09-04) repriced every SKU onto CHARM POINTS alongside V398's additive fee: x.99 in usd/eur/gbp, whole-rupee x99 in inr (₹599, ₹4,999 — paise-level .99 is not a price shape that market reads). `stripe-plans-ladder.test.ts` asserts the grid, the halving rule and every bound between the rungs; nothing here is an FX conversion of anything else.
$comment_tiers: Billing groups (spec 2026-07-21 §Pricing): a subscription covers several organisations, so each paid price is a GRADUATED tiered price whose quantity is the number of organisations in the group. Tier 1 is the plan base; tier 2+ is an extra organisation at half the base. `unit_amount`/`currency_options` stay in place and always equal tier 1 — they are what a group of one pays, and what the pricing page and lib/currency.ts advertise. Per-currency tier amounts are SET price points like every other amount here, derived as half the tier-1 point FLOORED TO THE CHARM GRID — the largest x.99 point at or below it, and for INR the largest whole-rupee x99 point (₹99, ₹199, ₹299 …) — never an FX conversion. REWORDED W3 (2026-09-04): it used to say “rounded DOWN to a whole major unit”, which stopped being true the moment the prices themselves became charm points — half of $14.99 is $7.495 and the rider is $6.99, not $7. A rule the seed does not obey is worse than no rule, because the next editor reprices to match the sentence. FLOOR, never round up: that is what keeps the “no more than half your plan’s rate” promise four locales make, and `stripe-plans-ladder.test.ts` now asserts the floored value EXACTLY, so a rider set too LOW is a fault as well — the shape a fat-fingered reprice actually takes, and the one an at-most-half bound welcomes.

product.name: Seazn Club Pro
product.description: Unlimited competitions, multi-division, online registration + entry fees, realtime scoreboard, custom branding, CSV/PDF exports. Covers up to 5 organisations on one bill — each extra organisation costs no more than half the base rate.

$comment_passes: Event Pass rungs (v17 #294): TWO one-time price points for the same single-competition upgrade, told apart ONLY by size — M ($11.99) is 10 divisions / 128 entrants per division, L ($44.99) is 20 divisions / 512 entrants. Everything else (features) is identical; the one-time AI credit grant is sized with the rung (PASS_CREDIT_GRANT: 25 on M, 35 on L — entitlements v18 W2 T5 sized it by rung, W2 T12 re-cut L from 50). `key` matches the `plans` row of the same name (M's key is literally `event_pass`, not `event_pass_m`), and the caps themselves live in plan_entitlements (V341 derives L's whole matrix from M's), never here — this file only owns the price. The rungs are bounded by the annual plan on both sides (3 × L >= annual keeps a third pass a nudge toward subscribing; 2 × L < annual keeps a two-tournament organiser out of one), and M is bounded ABOVE by one MONTH of Pro — added W3 after its absence let a dominated rung ship, M at $15 against Pro at $12/month, while every existing bound compared the rungs against the ANNUAL price and passed. Pass M is a strict subset of Pro on every axis the two share (10 divisions vs 20, 128 entrants vs 256, 4 stages vs 6, 5 restore points vs 10, 4% entry fee vs 2%), so a rung dearer than a month of the plan that dominates it is a product nobody rational buys. All of it is what stripe-plans-ladder.test.ts pins. stripe-sync loops this array by key and writes each price id into plans.stripe_price_id_onetime, so adding a rung needs no sync-script change; lib/currency.ts passPrice(currency, passKey) is the single reader.

$comment_packs: AI credit packs (v17 SPEC-2 §5/§6): one-time top-ups into the org/group's ai_credit_ledger wallet (bucket='pack', never-expire — D2). Not tied to a `plans` row, so the checkout route resolves the live price by `lookup_key` at request time (stripe.prices.list) instead of a stored id — stripe-sync.ts only needs to ensure the price exists, never write it back to a table. `credits` is our own field (never sent to Stripe) — the webhook grants the `credits` snapshot stamped into the session metadata at checkout creation (server-set, so it cannot be tampered with client-side); this catalog is only the logged fallback when the snapshot is absent (a drift the webhook staff-alerts, never a silent wrong/zero grant). The v18 reprice left every pack amount alone; they only lost their AUD point. W3 (2026-09-04) moved every OTHER SKU onto charm points and deliberately left these ROUND — $10, $25, $50, $100 — which design/v3/07 §3a marks as intentional in the same words: credits are compute, not packaging. A pack is bought as a quantity of a metered resource ($10 buys 40 credits), so $9.99 reads as a discount on a thing whose price is arithmetic, not as a keen price; the round number is what makes the per-credit rate legible. Recorded here because otherwise it reads as a section somebody forgot — `stripe-plans-ladder.test.ts` names `packs` as the one charm-grid exemption and asserts that the exempt set is exactly this one, so the exception cannot silently grow. The INR points were then RE-ANCHORED later in the same wave (2026-09-04) and are the only pack amounts that have ever moved: ₹799 / ₹1,999 / ₹3,999 / ₹7,999 became ₹399 / ₹999 / ₹1,999 / ₹3,999. The plans had been re-anchored to per-market set points while these were carried forward as 'unchanged', which left a dollar-priced SKU sitting in a rupee-priced catalogue. Measured against the per-credit rate Pro's own monthly price implies (that price divided by its `ai.credits.monthly` allowance), usd/eur/gbp bought pack credits at ~0.36-0.46x while India paid ~0.73-0.83x — twice the multiple, in every rung. Halving puts INR back on usd's multiple to within 0.15%. What is held equal across markets is the RATIO to the plan, never the amount: nothing here is an FX conversion of anything else. `stripe-plans-ladder.test.ts` now asserts that ratio in every currency, and that a pack never costs more per credit than the plan that includes credits — the comparison whose absence let the drift sit unseen, because every other rule in that file compares packaging to packaging.

$comment_seats: Extra-seat recurring add-on (v17 SPEC-2 §3/§11.3, Phase 3 Task 3a): a RECURRING $2/seat/month line item that rides the billing group's EXISTING subscription as an extra subscription item (stripe.subscriptionItems.create/.update, one invoice + one cycle + native proration — never a second subscription). quantity = seat count; each seat lifts members.max by delta_each (1). `feature_key`/`delta_each` are OUR fields (never sent to Stripe) — the customer.subscription.updated webhook (billing-events.syncSeatAddonsForSubscription) is the SINGLE writer of the resulting org_addons(feature_key='members.max', status='active') row, keyed idempotently on the subscription-item id. Like the packs there is no `plans` row: the seat usecase resolves the live price by `lookup_key` at request time (stripe.prices.list), so stripe-sync.ts only ensures the price exists. A flat per_unit RECURRING price (seats are per-org quantity, not a graduated group ladder); per-currency amounts are SET price points (v3/07 §4), never FX conversions. HIDDEN from customers since entitlements v18 R13: the price and the backend stay live and functional, but nothing advertises the add-on — there was never a purchase control, so hiding it is a copy change (the pricing page's add-on strip and content/help/billing/add-ons.md), not a code removal.

$comment_size_packs: Size-pack ONE-TIME add-on (v17 SPEC-2 §3/§11.3, Phase 3 Task 3b): a $5 one-time purchase that lifts ONE competition's entrants.per_division.max by delta_each (+32). Unlike the recurring seat it is a mode:'payment' Checkout Session (a competition is a bounded event, not recurring) with NO `interval` on the price. `feature_key`/`delta_each` are OUR fields (never sent to Stripe) — the checkout.session.completed webhook (billing-events.grantSizePackAddon) is the SINGLE writer of the resulting org_addons(target_competition_id, feature_key='entrants.per_division.max', status='active') row, keyed idempotently on the PAYMENT_INTENT id (a one-time pack has no subscription item). The pack SHAPE is admin-editable via the size_pack_catalog DB table (V325); this entry is only the code-seeded default + the Stripe-owned price. Like the packs there is no `plans` row: the checkout resolves the live price by `lookup_key` at request time (stripe.prices.list), so stripe-sync.ts only ensures the price exists. Per-currency amounts mirror the pro monthly rider's scale (the same $5 price point), SET points (v3/07 §4), never FX conversions.

$comment_org_addons: Extra-organisation RECURRING add-on (v17 gap remediation #293, design/v17-pricing-entitlements SPEC-2 §3/§7): exceeding the group's plan cap (orgs.max_owned) is a PURCHASE, not an upgrade wall. Priced identically to the plan's own graduated tier-2 rate (extraOrgPrice() in lib/currency.ts reads the SAME plans[].prices.monthly.tiers[up_to=inf] numbers this seed copies) — org-addon-catalog-parity.test.ts pins the two together so a tier change and a forgotten add-on price can never drift apart. Like extra_seat this rides the group's EXISTING subscription as an extra RECURRING item (never a second subscription, never annual — always $/month regardless of the group's own billing interval, mirroring extra_seat's shape exactly). ONE ENTRY PER SELF-SERVE PLAN: entitlements v18 leaves exactly one (Pro), because Community has no subscription for a rider to ride and Enterprise is not sold self-serve. The array shape stays per-plan rather than collapsing to a single price, since the rate is a property of the plan's own tier ladder and must move with it. `plan_key`/`feature_key`/`delta_each` are OUR fields (never sent to Stripe) — the customer.subscription.updated webhook (billing-events.syncOrgAddonsForSubscription) is the SINGLE writer of the resulting org_addons(feature_key='orgs.max_owned', target_org_id=null) row, group-wide (not scoped to one org, unlike a seat). Flat per_unit prices (quantity = extra orgs bought), not a graduated ladder: the plan price already carries the group ladder.
